original_question: Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G. Is it always possible to choose three pairwise-disjoint proper L-colorings, that is, three proper colorings from the given vertex lists such that each vertex receives three different colors across the three colorings?
target_in_paper: Section 2, subsection "Planar bipartite graphs", Problem 2.4, with notation from the opening definitions of Section 2.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main numbered open problem very closely: it uses the same graph class stated in Problem 2.4 (cubic planar graph), the same input data (a 3-list-assignment), and the same goal (three pairwise-disjoint proper colorings from the given lists). Your parenthetical explanation also correctly spells out the intended vertexwise disjointness condition across the three colorings.
missing_details: State the universal quantifiers explicitly: the question is whether this holds for every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L on G.
Define a 3-list-assignment formally: each vertex v is assigned a list L(v) of exactly 3 colors (in the paper, colors are taken from N).
Define an L-coloring formally: a map c on V(G) with c(v) in L(v) for every vertex v.
State properness formally: for each edge uv in E(G), one requires c(u) != c(v) within each coloring.
State disjointness formally for the whole triple: for every vertex v, the three values c1(v), c2(v), c3(v) are pairwise distinct.
If full self-containment is desired, say that cubic means 3-regular.

The paper places Problem 2.4 inside the subsection titled "Planar bipartite graphs" and immediately afterward mentions the cubic bipartite case separately; your draft does not mention this nearby contextual ambiguity.
refined_question: For every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L on G (that is, each vertex v in V(G) is assigned a 3-element list L(v) of colors), do there always exist three proper L-colorings c1, c2, c3 of G such that ci(v) is in L(v) for every vertex v and every i in {1,2,3}, ci(u) != ci(v) for every edge uv in E(G), and for each vertex v the three colors c1(v), c2(v), c3(v) are pairwise distinct?

Section 2 first defines list-assignments, L-colorings, properness, and disjointness, and then, under the subsection "Planar bipartite graphs", asks: "Is it possible to choose three disjoint proper colourings?" for a 3-list-assignment of a cubic planar graph. Your draft already matches that question almost verbatim, so the main refinement is to make all quantifiers and definitions explicit. I did not replace it with the broader nearby question about planar graphs in general, nor with the later unnumbered cubic bipartite variant; I only flag that surrounding context as a paper-level ambiguity.
